text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
British marine DAVID COLLINS, who arrived in Australia with the First Fleet and later became the first Governor of Tasmania, was born on this day in 1756.
ABRAM-LOUIS BUVELOT was born in Switzerland in 1814, and later became a landscape artist in South Australia. No text received
American industrialist and inventor of the luxury railway-carriage, GEORGE PULLMAN, was born in 1831.
The inventor of the telephone, Scottish-born American ALEXANDER GRAHAM BELL, was born in 1847.
Australian psychiatrist, medical hypnotist and author AINSLIE MEARES was born in 1910.
American actress and sex symbol JEAN HARLOW was born in 1911.
Australian historian CHARLES MANNING CLARK was born on this day in 1915.
Swiss-born American actress URSULA ANDRESS, was born in 1936.
US bass player and singer with 'Dr Hook' JANCE GARFAT was born in 1944.
UK drummer with 'Adam And The Ants' CHRISTOPHER HUGHES was born in 1954.
** EVENTS **
1869 : WILLIAM LANNEY (known as "King Billy"), the last full-blood Tasmanian Aborigine, died.
1923 : "TIME" magazine was launched in the United States, edited by HENRY R. LUCE.
1931 : 117 years after it was written, the "Star Spangled Banner" was adopted as the American national anthem.

1933 : The likelihood of a link between sunburn and cancer was made public at a conference in Canberra. The national Cancer conference called for public education programmes to alert people to the dangers of sunburn. Health authorities were told that they should issue warnings to people who spent a lot of time outdoors for recreation or work.
1939 : The American western "STAGECOACH" starring JOHN WAYNE in his first major screen role, premiered in New York.
1950 : The US Congress voted to admit Alaska as the 49th State.
1959 : LOU COSTELLO, the comedy partner of BUD ABBOTT, died.
1974 : A Turkish Airlines DC10 crashed into a forest near Paris, killing all 344 people on board.
1985 : Striking British miners voted to return to work after a year-long stoppage, which had been seen as an act of defiance against rime Minister MARGARET THATCHER.
1987 : DANNY KAYE died of heart failure. He was 74.
1991 : QUEEN ELIZABETH II needed 3 stitches in her finger, after being hurt trying to break-up a fight between the Royal corgi dogs!

1994 : Former Federal Opposition leader JOHN HEWSON came out in support of the gay and lesbian mardi-gras in Sydney. He had several opponents within the coaltion but defended his position by saying the Liberal Party was for all Australians.
